status: One regular proposal; two literal Story holds and three concise discovery/canon holds. Zero author admissions.

candidates.subject: panther chameleon
candidates.title: Back above ground
candidates.body:
I kept trying to hold the ground.

My front feet closed on earth. It broke apart. I pushed it behind me and took another grip. By the time the hole was deep enough, my tail was curled tightly around nothing.

Went backward into the dark. For a while there was only the wall against my sides and the slow work inside me.

When I came out, the eggs stayed below.

I pushed earth into the opening. More earth. The place grew flat and stopped looking like a place I had been.

At the first branch I reached, my tail went round before either front foot. For a while I stayed with all five grips closed.
candidates.visibleScene: Pink-brown female panther chameleon faces out of excavated soil. Head and forelimbs are exposed, rear body is partly concealed in the hole, and the long tail rises behind her with its tip curled. No eggs are visible.
candidates.fictionBoundary: The observer explicitly identifies a female digging and laying eggs. The exact failed grips, feeling of enclosure, timing, backfilling and return to a branch are fictional temporal development around that documented reproductive event. Independent field observation supports excavation, turning outward for laying, backfilling and subsequent ascent. No claim that this still photographs the eggs or the later branch.
candidates.canon: Existing adult female Cora, Ambanja forest edge Madagascar (-13.686,48.464). Preserve avatar and all ten literal prior passages. This is a first proposed reproductive event, not offspring care or a new home. Ankarana is photographic provenance only. Add as an adult episode; no juvenile order constraint, egg count, fertility, mate, hatching or offspring survival asserted.
candidates.payoff: Her familiar five grips cannot hold the earth she must enter. After burying the eggs and concealing her own trace, she returns to wood and keeps every grip closed. The changed bodily use carries the vulnerability without a stated lesson.
candidates.reviewFlag: Sharp subject and unusual documented event; flash flattens some soil texture. The slow reflective ending deliberately does not supply a quip. Lead should judge whether the physical return has enough emotional weight for regular admission.

holds.title: Too many stems
holds.body:
Dropped out of the pine and landed under the grass.

Raised a leg. A stem came with it. Put the leg down and tried another.

I've stopped trying to jump. First I need enough room to stand.
holds.reason: Literal draft evaluated, not recommended. The exact male-like black-and-white spider lies among crossing stems, but no attachment is demonstrated. The invented snag supplies almost all the incident and produces another bodily obstruction task. Source mentions a silk descent but these images show its aftermath only. No independent adult-sex determination completed, so no canon admission proposed.

holds.title: Outside again
holds.body:
The smooth wall ended under my front feet. Beyond it, leaves.

I stayed on the edge until a caterpillar moved. Then all eight feet agreed to leave.
holds.reason: Literal draft evaluated, not recommended. Soft portrait on a human-made cubicle edge does not show the subsequently reported caterpillar. Prose amounts to a generic departure for food and spends its payoff offscreen. Do not promote based on source caption alone.
Sharp immature portraits before a molt; none shows molting or exuviae. No new molting narrative drafted from these.
Observer explicitly identifies newly molted dark-form female. Wrong sex for existing male Ludo despite black coloration.
Read full current arc. Full-fan courtship is already admitted. Licensed discovery did not yield a distinct scene warranting more downloads in this batch. No photo claim or quota entry.

biologySources.title: Evidence of spatiotemporal planning in a panther chameleon (Furcifer pardalis) on the Masoala Peninsula, Madagascar
biologySources.author: Timothy M. Eppley
biologySources.evidence: Primary field observation on page 909: female excavates, turns outward and deposits eggs, backfills using front and hind limbs, pats soil and ascends canopy. Used only for this physical sequence. The unusual older-clutch discovery and speculative planning interpretation are not incorporated into fiction.
